project.name: Retail POS Website
project.product_context: Offline-first Flutter Android retail POS intended for Pakistan SMBs and general stores; product capabilities and release status must be verified against the real app before being advertised.
source_of_requirements: Research corrections agreed in the conversation
Architecture decisions agreed in the conversation
Current app repository and implementation evidence, to be audited before product claims are published
project.baseline_status: Website foundation committed on feature branch; draft PR open; CI did not produce step logs, so production build is not yet verified. No deployment, APK publication, or database connection has occurred.

checklist_conventions.completion_rule: Mark an item completed only when its acceptance criteria have been checked and evidence is recorded. Planned features, draft code, and untested builds do not count as shipped.

repository_and_data.mobile_app_repository: Keep the existing Flutter app repository separate and do not expose private app source through the website.
repository_and_data.website_repository: Use this separate repository for static website code, content, docs, and website QA.
repository_and_data.release_distribution: Use a separate public release repository or another verified public release-asset location for approved signed APKs and the update manifest. Keep app source private.
repository_and_data.website_database: No database for the initial website. Keep public pages, FAQ, policies, and changelog in version-controlled files.
rationale: Avoid exposing retail sales, customer, supplier, ledger, or other private POS data.
Avoid backend/database costs and maintenance for a primarily informational website.
Keep app source, public marketing content, and public binary distribution responsibilities separate.

hosting.preferred_initial_host: Netlify Free, subject to verifying current terms, commercial-use eligibility, limits, and GitHub integration before connecting.
hosting.custom_domain: Do not purchase a domain initially; use the host-provided HTTPS subdomain.
hosting.spending_policy: Do not start paid services, upgrade a plan, buy a domain, enable auto-recharge, or incur costs without explicit user approval.
hosting.fallback_rule: If the selected free host's current terms or limits do not fit the project, pause and evaluate another genuinely free commercial-eligible static host before deployment.

technology.proposed_stack: Astro + TypeScript, statically generated pages, Markdown/JSON content where suitable.
technology.content_management: Version-controlled source content; no paid CMS.
technology.architecture_rule: Prefer static HTML and minimal client-side JavaScript. Add server functions only if a real requirement emerges and the user approves the extra complexity.

product_truth.launch_positioning: Pre-launch / pilot status until an approved public release is actually available.
product_truth.claims_policy: Every product capability, security statement, metric, compatibility claim, and release note must be supported by code, test results, or verified product evidence.
product_truth.proof_policy: No fake testimonials, fake customer counts, fabricated ratings, invented screenshots, or claims of production readiness without evidence.

items.requirement: Keep the website in this separate repository.
items.acceptance_criteria: Website source and public content are maintained in retail-pos-website; no unrelated app source is copied into it.

items.requirement: Keep the Flutter app source repository separate and private unless the owner explicitly changes that decision.
items.acceptance_criteria: No secrets or private application source are exposed through the public website or release assets.

items.requirement: Do not create a website database for launch.
items.acceptance_criteria: The initial site renders from repository content and has no database credentials, database migrations, or POS database connection.

items.requirement: Keep the website completely disconnected from the POS production database.
items.acceptance_criteria: Build and runtime configuration contain no Supabase service-role key, production database password, or direct POS-data access.

items.requirement: Define a separate public release-asset location for signed APKs and update metadata.
items.acceptance_criteria: The intended public manifest and APK URLs are documented and can be accessed without private GitHub authentication.

items.requirement: Use a static-first architecture with minimal JavaScript.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pages are useful and crawlable in their initial HTML; JavaScript is only added where it materially improves a real workflow.

items.requirement: Confirm hosting terms before deployment.
items.acceptance_criteria: Current commercial-use terms, free-plan limits, deployment behavior, bandwidth/build limits, and account requirements are checked and recorded.

items.requirement: Keep spending at zero unless the user explicitly approves otherwise.
items.acceptance_criteria: No paid plan, paid domain, paid service, or automatic billing/recharge is enabled.

items.requirement: Document architecture and release ownership.
items.acceptance_criteria: README explains website repository, public release assets, deployment process, and which repository owns each responsibility.

items.requirement: Use reviewable, small changes with explicit release gates.
items.acceptance_criteria: Changes are validated before deployment; no mobile-app PR merge, production migration, or APK publication occurs without required approval.

items.requirement: Audit the actual Flutter app and repository before writing definitive feature claims.
items.acceptance_criteria: A feature inventory links each advertised capability to source code, tests, a working screen, or other reproducible evidence.

items.requirement: Classify each capability as implemented-and-verified, implemented-but-untested, in progress, planned, or unavailable.
items.acceptance_criteria: The website content distinguishes all statuses and never presents planned work as shipped.

items.requirement: Verify the actual Android package identity and release version.
items.acceptance_criteria: Package ID, app display name, version, build number, signing identity, and minimum Android version are read from the app configuration/build evidence.

items.requirement: Verify actual offline behavior before describing it.
items.acceptance_criteria: Content names which workflows work offline, which need connectivity, what is queued, and how failures/retries are surfaced.

items.requirement: Document offline multi-device stock limitations honestly.
items.acceptance_criteria: The site explains that disconnected devices cannot instantly see each other's sales and describes only the reconciliation behavior that is actually implemented.

items.requirement: Verify the roles and permissions that actually exist.
items.acceptance_criteria: Owner, manager, cashier, or other role labels are only published if supported by app permissions and tests.

items.requirement: Verify product-specific details such as PKR, barcode, units, receipts, reports, and supplier/customer workflows.
items.acceptance_criteria: Every published detail is supported by code or test evidence; unknown items remain unclaimed.

items.requirement: Maintain a source-of-truth product capability matrix.
items.acceptance_criteria: A repository document records feature name, status, evidence, last verification date, and approved public wording.

items.requirement: Create a clear homepage.
items.acceptance_criteria: The homepage explains what the product is, who it is for, its current availability/status, and the next useful action.

items.requirement: Create a product/features hub.
items.acceptance_criteria: The hub summarizes verified capabilities and links to relevant deeper explanations.

items.requirement: Create a dedicated download/get-app page.
items.acceptance_criteria: It states whether a public build is available and includes version, requirements, and installation guidance when applicable.

items.requirement: Create a changelog/release-history page.
items.acceptance_criteria: The page lists only real, published releases in newest-first order.

items.requirement: Create FAQ and support information.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visitors can find clear answers and a verified contact/support route.

items.requirement: Create privacy and terms pages before public launch.
items.acceptance_criteria: Policies reflect actual data collection, external services, distribution, and jurisdictional needs and are reviewed before publication.

items.requirement: Create a security/data-handling page.
items.acceptance_criteria: It explains verified roles, device admission, storage, sync, backups, and limitations without unsupported guarantees.

items.requirement: Create a page or section explaining offline operation and sync.
items.acceptance_criteria: The explanation differentiates local behavior, network-dependent behavior, retry/recovery, and conflict handling.

items.requirement: Create About and Contact pages or equivalent sections.
items.acceptance_criteria: Product identity and support details are confirmed and consistent across the site.

items.requirement: Create pricing/access information only after the actual model is decided.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visitors can understand whether access is free, paid, invite-only, or pilot-based; no invented price is published.

items.requirement: Add feature deep pages for high-intent workflows when verified content exists.
items.acceptance_criteria: Checkout, till, inventory, offline/sync, or other pages provide distinct useful detail rather than thin duplicate SEO pages.

items.requirement: Add role/use-case pages only when they reflect real supported workflows.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cashier, manager, owner, kiryana, or general-store pages contain unique accurate information and not just keyword substitutions.

items.requirement: Consider comparisons, integrations, case studies, status page, and help center at scale.
items.acceptance_criteria: Each is added only when there is genuine information and a maintainable operational need.

items.requirement: Write an outcome-led hero headline.
items.acceptance_criteria: A first-time visitor can understand the product and intended audience without reading technical jargon.

items.requirement: Show the current pilot/pre-launch status clearly.
items.acceptance_criteria: The hero or immediately visible content does not imply public production readiness if the release is not approved.

items.requirement: Use one dominant primary call to action.
items.acceptance_criteria: The primary action is appropriate to the real state: approved download, pilot/contact request, or product walkthrough.

items.requirement: Use real product evidence instead of invented interface visuals.
items.acceptance_criteria: Any product screenshot, GIF, or demo is captured from an actual build and accurately represents current behavior.

items.requirement: Explain the customer problem in recognizable terms.
items.acceptance_criteria: The content addresses real retail concerns such as cash reconciliation, stock accuracy, connectivity, or device access only where relevant.

items.requirement: Present three to five verified outcome/feature highlights.
items.acceptance_criteria: Each highlight follows outcome → feature → mechanism → proof and links to supporting detail.

items.requirement: Include a compact trust signal without fabricated social proof.
items.acceptance_criteria: Use verified pilot status, actual product evidence, or a truthful statement about intended users instead of invented logos, reviews, or metrics.

items.requirement: Explain access/pricing or the current pilot path.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visitors are not left guessing how to try the product or whether it is publicly available.

items.requirement: End with a clear next action and a concise privacy/security reassurance.
items.acceptance_criteria: The action works and reassurance is factual and linked to fuller details.

items.requirement: Use outcome → feature → mechanism → proof for each promoted capability.
items.acceptance_criteria: Every feature page/section explains the benefit, what happens, how it works, and evidence or a clearly disclosed limitation.

items.requirement: Explain checkout and payment methods only as implemented.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cash, online, credit/split payments, PKR rounding, receipt numbering, and retry/idempotency behavior are individually verified before claims.

items.requirement: Explain catalogue and inventory behavior only as implemented.
items.acceptance_criteria: Barcode/SKU search, units such as kg/piece, stock balances, low-stock rules, product publishing, and stock movements are evidence-backed.

items.requirement: Explain till and cash control only as implemented.
items.acceptance_criteria: Open/close, expected-versus-actual cash, cash-in/out, movement history, and shift reporting are verified.

items.requirement: Explain roles and device admission only as implemented.
items.acceptance_criteria: Permissions, device admission/revocation, device limits, and recovery steps match the actual application.

items.requirement: Explain offline and synchronization workflows.
items.acceptance_criteria: Pending operations, retries, conflict handling, recovery, and reconciliation are described without promising impossible simultaneous offline consistency.

items.requirement: Explain customer/supplier ledgers and purchase workflows if verified.
items.acceptance_criteria: Linked transactions, balances, supplier history, purchase receipt, and related reports match the real app.

items.requirement: Explain receipts and sharing if verified.
items.acceptance_criteria: Receipt persistence, digital/PNG output, and native sharing behavior are tested and accurately described.

items.requirement: Explain reports and reporting periods if verified.
items.acceptance_criteria: Report definitions, date ranges, time zones, and Pakistan calendar-period behavior are accurate.

items.requirement: Provide role-aware workflow paths or a short walkthrough.
items.acceptance_criteria: Cashier, manager, and owner journeys use real screens and do not reveal unsupported or private data.

checklist.title: Official Android download and in-app updates

items.requirement: Do not expose a public APK until an approved signed release exists.
items.acceptance_criteria: Download page shows a truthful unavailable/pilot state until release approval and validation are complete.

items.requirement: Use a public release asset location separate from the private app source.
items.acceptance_criteria: Anonymous visitors can fetch the approved APK and manifest without repository login.

items.requirement: Display exact app version, build number, release date, and release status.
items.acceptance_criteria: Displayed metadata matches the APK and release record.

items.requirement: Verify the release is signed with the expected production signing key.
items.acceptance_criteria: Release signature/package identity is validated; debug builds are never labelled as public releases.

items.requirement: Preserve signing-key continuity across updates.
items.acceptance_criteria: A newer APK installs as an update over the prior approved app without changing package identity or signing identity.

items.requirement: Publish a SHA-256 checksum for each APK.
items.acceptance_criteria: The published checksum is generated from the exact uploaded asset and can be independently verified.

items.requirement: Document Android compatibility and installation requirements.
items.acceptance_criteria: Minimum supported Android version and relevant permissions are read from build configuration and tested.

items.requirement: Explain Android's install-from-this-source permission and installer confirmation.
items.acceptance_criteria: Instructions explain that Android may require user permission and confirmation; no silent-install promise is made.

items.requirement: Define a stable HTTPS update-manifest URL.
items.acceptance_criteria: The URL is stable, publicly reachable, returns valid JSON, and is configured consistently in the release build.

items.requirement: Validate manifest schema and monotonic version/build behavior.
items.acceptance_criteria: Version, build number, minimum supported build, release notes, APK URL, and checksum are validated; downgrade/invalid metadata is rejected.

items.requirement: Harden the updater's download URL and redirect handling.
items.acceptance_criteria: Only HTTPS is allowed; redirects are handled safely with an explicit host allowlist or an approved same-origin asset strategy; arbitrary hosts and downgrade redirects are rejected.

items.requirement: Verify the APK checksum before opening Android's installer.
items.acceptance_criteria: A corrupt, truncated, mismatched, or oversized APK is rejected and the user receives a clear error.

items.requirement: Test optional and mandatory update behavior.
items.acceptance_criteria: Optional updates can be deferred; mandatory updates respect the configured minimum build; manifest/network failures do not falsely claim success.

items.requirement: Test first-install and subsequent-update journeys on real Android hardware.
items.acceptance_criteria: The first install and at least one signed in-app update are validated on the supported device path before public launch.

items.requirement: Document recovery for failed or interrupted updates.
items.acceptance_criteria: Users can retry safely, retain the installed version if a download fails, and find support guidance.

items.requirement: Ensure website download metadata and update manifest remain consistent.
items.acceptance_criteria: Automated or release-checklist validation catches mismatched versions, build numbers, checksums, and URLs.

checklist.title: Changelog, release history, and release discipline

items.requirement: Use newest-first release entries with a date and version/build.
items.acceptance_criteria: Every published entry maps to a real approved release.

items.requirement: Use consistent change types such as Added, Improved/Changed, Fixed, and Security.
items.acceptance_criteria: Labels are understandable and used consistently; they do not imply a security fix without evidence.

items.requirement: Write customer-facing benefit summaries before technical details.
items.acceptance_criteria: A store owner can understand the effect without reading commit messages.

items.requirement: Separate user-facing changes from compatibility/migration notes.
items.acceptance_criteria: Any required action, supported-version change, data migration, or known issue is clear.

items.requirement: Do not list unmerged code or unpublished builds as released.
items.acceptance_criteria: Release entries are added only after the exact signed APK has passed the release gate and is publicly available.

items.requirement: Use visuals for UI changes when real screenshots are available.
items.acceptance_criteria: Images show the actual version and do not contain customer data or invented UI.

items.requirement: Maintain a realistic update cadence.
items.acceptance_criteria: Publish notes when shipping meaningful changes; never invent activity to fill a schedule.

checklist.title: Visual consistency, responsive UX, and product showcase

items.requirement: Inspect actual Flutter theme tokens before finalizing website styling.
items.acceptance_criteria: Colors, typography, surfaces, radius, elevation, and icon language are extracted from the current app/theme rather than guessed.

items.requirement: Make the site feel like the product's front door.
items.acceptance_criteria: Website color and component language is consistent with the real app and does not introduce an unrelated generic SaaS aesthetic.

items.requirement: Use mobile-first layouts.
items.acceptance_criteria: Core content and actions work on narrow screens without horizontal scrolling or clipped controls.

items.requirement: Make primary tap targets at least approximately 44 by 44 CSS pixels where practical.
items.acceptance_criteria: Navigation, CTAs, accordions, and other controls are comfortable to use on touchscreens.

items.requirement: Use progressive disclosure for long content.
items.acceptance_criteria: Summaries come first; technical detail, setup steps, and edge cases are grouped or expandable without hiding essential safety information.

items.requirement: Use real product screenshots in device frames where useful.
items.acceptance_criteria: Screenshots come from a real build, are legible, and reflect supported features.

items.requirement: Create a short ungated product walkthrough before considering a full interactive demo center.
items.acceptance_criteria: A visitor can see meaningful value without providing an email; demo failure has a clear fallback.

items.requirement: Organize demos by real jobs or roles if the product evidence supports them.
items.acceptance_criteria: Walkthroughs cover genuine workflows such as running a shift, closeout, or device recovery—not fabricated capabilities.

items.requirement: Keep motion subtle and purposeful.
items.acceptance_criteria: Animations do not block navigation, harm readability, or create performance/accessibility problems.

items.requirement: Provide visible loading, empty, error, and unavailable states where the website has interactive functionality.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visitors always have a clear next step when an asset, demo, or download is unavailable.

checklist.title: Trust, privacy, security, legal, and support

items.requirement: Publish accurate privacy information before collecting personal data or releasing publicly.
items.acceptance_criteria: The policy describes actual data collection, cookies/analytics, external services, contact flows, retention, and relevant rights.

items.requirement: Publish terms appropriate to the actual distribution and access model.
items.acceptance_criteria: Terms do not promise services, warranties, support, or availability that are not offered.

items.requirement: Do not claim encryption, certifications, compliance, backups, or security guarantees without verification.
items.acceptance_criteria: Every security statement links to a real implementation or documented operational control.

items.requirement: Explain role-based access and device controls accurately.
items.acceptance_criteria: Role boundaries, admission, revocation, and device limits match verified behavior.

items.requirement: Explain what data the website itself collects.
items.acceptance_criteria: The initial static site does not imply it can see POS transactions; no POS customer/sales data is transmitted to it.

items.requirement: Keep secrets out of source and client bundles.
items.acceptance_criteria: No API keys, private tokens, database credentials, signing keys, or secrets are committed or shipped to browsers.

items.requirement: Provide a real support route and realistic expectations.
items.acceptance_criteria: Contact links are tested and response-time promises are made only if an actual support commitment exists.

items.requirement: Do not publish fake testimonials, customer logos, star ratings, or outcome statistics.
items.acceptance_criteria: All social proof is attributable and permissioned, or replaced with factual product evidence.

items.requirement: Review privacy/legal content for Pakistan and any other actual target markets.
items.acceptance_criteria: Policies are reviewed for actual operations and are not presented as legal advice or copied boilerplate that contradicts the product.

checklist.title: SEO, GEO/AEO, crawlability, and content quality

items.requirement: Give each important page a descriptive, unique title and meta description.
items.acceptance_criteria: Titles and descriptions reflect actual page content and are not duplicated across the site.

items.requirement: Use crawlable semantic HTML and a logical heading hierarchy.
items.acceptance_criteria: Main content is available in rendered HTML and headings describe the page structure.

items.requirement: Use clean, stable URLs.
items.acceptance_criteria: Routes are descriptive, lowercase where appropriate, and do not change without redirects.

items.requirement: Add a sitemap and correctly configured robots.txt.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sitemap contains canonical public pages; robots.txt does not accidentally block the site.

items.requirement: Add canonical URLs and Open Graph/social metadata.
items.acceptance_criteria: Canonical links and social preview metadata point to the correct deployed URL once selected.

items.requirement: Add meaningful image alt text.
items.acceptance_criteria: Informative images have descriptive alt text; decorative images use empty alt text.

items.requirement: Add structured data only where accurate and eligible.
items.acceptance_criteria: Organization, SoftwareApplication, BreadcrumbList, or other schema validates and matches visible content; no rich-result guarantee is made.

items.requirement: Structure FAQ answers to answer the question first.
items.acceptance_criteria: Each answer begins with a direct, quotable response and then gives limitations or context.

items.requirement: Follow Google's current AI-feature/search guidance rather than GEO hacks.
items.acceptance_criteria: No claims that special AI markup, llms.txt, or keyword stuffing guarantees AI citations; content is useful, accurate, and crawlable.

items.requirement: Build internal links between hubs, feature pages, download, changelog, FAQ, and trust pages.
items.acceptance_criteria: Visitors and crawlers can navigate related content without dead ends.

items.requirement: Create Pakistan/location-specific pages only where the product genuinely serves that audience.
items.acceptance_criteria: No thin city pages or unsupported local-service claims are published.

items.requirement: Publish educational resources when useful content can be maintained.
items.acceptance_criteria: Articles answer real retail POS questions and cite reliable sources for external factual claims.

items.requirement: Verify indexability after deployment.
items.acceptance_criteria: Production pages return expected status codes, canonical URLs, and are not blocked by noindex or host settings.

items.requirement: Aim for Core Web Vitals targets at the 75th percentile: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1.
items.acceptance_criteria: Lab testing is used before launch; field data is monitored when enough real traffic exists.

items.requirement: Keep JavaScript and third-party assets to a minimum.
items.acceptance_criteria: The site has no unnecessary client frameworks, autoplay media, or heavy external scripts.

items.requirement: Optimize images and fonts.
items.acceptance_criteria: Images use suitable dimensions/formats, fonts are limited, and layout shifts from assets are prevented.

items.requirement: Check keyboard navigation and visible focus states.
items.acceptance_criteria: All navigation and interactive controls are usable without a mouse.

items.requirement: Check contrast, labels, semantic controls, and reduced motion.
items.acceptance_criteria: Important text and controls are accessible; form fields have labels; motion respects user preferences.

items.requirement: Test responsive layouts across phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
items.acceptance_criteria: Navigation, typography, feature layouts, changelog, and download sections remain usable at common viewport sizes.

items.requirement: Check console errors, broken assets, and failed network requests.
items.acceptance_criteria: No unexplained errors remain in production-like builds.

items.requirement: Run HTML/link, accessibility, and Lighthouse-style audits.
items.acceptance_criteria: Critical and high-severity issues are fixed or explicitly documented before release.

items.requirement: Verify Netlify Free's current terms and limits before linking the repository.
items.acceptance_criteria: Commercial eligibility, monthly credits/limits, build behavior, bandwidth, and pause behavior are documented from current official sources.

items.requirement: Use the free host-provided HTTPS subdomain initially.
items.acceptance_criteria: No paid domain is purchased or required for initial testing.

items.requirement: Connect GitHub deployment with least privilege.
items.acceptance_criteria: The host can deploy the website repository without access to unrelated repositories or secrets beyond what is needed.

items.requirement: Configure production and preview deployments safely.
items.acceptance_criteria: Preview changes can be reviewed before production; failed builds do not replace the last working site unexpectedly.

items.requirement: Confirm HTTPS and correct redirects.
items.acceptance_criteria: All public URLs use HTTPS, canonical redirects are consistent, and no redirect loops exist.

items.requirement: Avoid paid features and automatic billing.
items.acceptance_criteria: Account settings are reviewed to ensure no paid add-ons, auto-recharge, or spending commitment is activated.

items.requirement: Document deployment and rollback steps.
items.acceptance_criteria: A maintainer can redeploy a known good commit and recover from a broken release.

items.requirement: Monitor free-plan usage and build failures.
items.acceptance_criteria: Usage can be checked periodically and there is a documented response if the free quota is reached.

items.requirement: Keep environment variables minimal.
items.acceptance_criteria: Static pages need no secret environment variables; any public build variables are explicitly documented as public.

items.requirement: Document how to change the public base URL later.
items.acceptance_criteria: Canonical URLs, sitemap, social metadata, and update-manifest links can be updated without hidden hard-coded old domains.

items.requirement: Validate JSON, TypeScript, and the production static build.
items.acceptance_criteria: Build and validation commands pass from a clean checkout.

items.requirement: Test all internal and external links.
items.acceptance_criteria: No broken navigation, download, support, policy, or changelog links remain.

items.requirement: Review every product claim against the capability matrix.
items.acceptance_criteria: No planned or untested capability is described as currently available.

items.requirement: Test download page with no release available.
items.acceptance_criteria: The empty/pilot state is informative and does not present placeholder or private URLs as real downloads.

items.requirement: Test the download page after a real approved release is available.
items.acceptance_criteria: APK URL, version/build, checksum, size, requirements, release notes, and signature status all agree.

items.requirement: Validate the public update manifest against the app's expected schema.
items.acceptance_criteria: Manifest fields, HTTPS URLs, version policy, minimum supported build, checksum, and host restrictions pass automated tests.

items.requirement: Test updater failure paths.
items.acceptance_criteria: Network failure, invalid JSON, redirect to unapproved host, checksum mismatch, partial download, and installer cancellation all have safe outcomes.

items.requirement: Validate the update flow on actual Android hardware.
items.acceptance_criteria: A signed update is installed over the prior signed build on the intended supported device path; emulator-only results are not described as device validation.

items.requirement: Review mobile UX and accessibility manually.
items.acceptance_criteria: Primary CTA, menus, download instructions, FAQ, and error states are usable on a phone.

items.requirement: Review privacy, terms, contact information, and support links.
items.acceptance_criteria: All are accurate and functional before public launch.

items.requirement: Confirm SEO basics and production URL configuration.
items.acceptance_criteria: Sitemap, robots.txt, canonical links, metadata, social cards, and structured data point to the actual production host.

items.requirement: Record known limitations and unresolved issues.
items.acceptance_criteria: No known blocker is hidden; remaining non-blockers have an owner and follow-up plan.

items.requirement: Do not claim a public launch before the release gates pass.
items.acceptance_criteria: Launch announcement and public download activation happen only after explicit review of all P0 gates.

items.requirement: Defer interactive demo center until real product screens and workflows are available.
items.acceptance_criteria: A short real walkthrough is considered first; full interactive demos require demonstrated value and maintainable assets.

items.requirement: Defer customer case studies and testimonials until genuine customers give permission.
items.acceptance_criteria: No placeholder testimonials are published.

items.requirement: Defer blog/resources until there is capacity to maintain accurate useful content.
items.acceptance_criteria: Content plan targets real user questions rather than volume or keyword stuffing.

items.requirement: Defer comparison pages and integration directories until the claims can be substantiated.
items.acceptance_criteria: Comparisons are fair, dated, sourced where appropriate, and do not rely on disparagement.

items.requirement: Defer a status page unless the product has real services/uptime worth reporting.
items.acceptance_criteria: Status is not simulated or presented as live without a monitored source.

items.requirement: Defer email capture, accounts, contact-form storage, analytics, and a CMS unless there is a real need.
items.acceptance_criteria: Any later collection has explicit approval, a privacy review, and an appropriate secure implementation.

items.requirement: Consider a custom domain only after the user explicitly approves the cost and ownership.
items.acceptance_criteria: No domain purchase occurs as part of the initial free launch.

launch_acceptance_gate: The website builds successfully from a clean checkout.
The site is responsive, accessible, and has no unresolved critical or high-severity QA defects.
All product claims are backed by current evidence and the pilot/public status is unmistakable.
Privacy, terms, support, and contact information are accurate.
The site is served over HTTPS and is crawlable with correct canonical metadata, sitemap, and robots.txt.
No production POS database, private source, customer data, signing key, or secret is exposed.
No public APK is linked until a signed release has passed the release gate.
The update manifest and APK checksum/host/version rules are validated before updater activation.
No paid service, domain, auto-recharge, or spending commitment has been activated without explicit approval.
The owner has been given the deployment URL, repository changes, QA results, and known limitations.

source_references_to_recheck_before_laun.check_before_launch: Confirm current recommendations for crawlability, page titles, links, and useful content.
Confirm current advice for appearing in AI search features; do not promise citations or use unsupported hacks.
Confirm current thresholds and evaluation guidance.
Use as a changelog convention, not as proof that a release exists.
Confirm current binary asset constraints and public download behavior.
Confirm current installation permissions and user confirmation behavior for the target Android versions.
Confirm current free-plan limits, commercial eligibility, build quotas, and whether a site pauses at its limit.
